title: Playwright's launch-time check tells you to run the command that wastes the disk
appliesTo: Sandboxes that preinstall browsers at PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH, where the npm-resolved playwright version expects a different browser revision than the one present.
claim: Installing the playwright npm package into an environment that already ships browsers produces a launch-time failure whose remedy text instructs you to run `npx playwright install` — the exact action that re-downloads hundreds of megabytes into a directory the environment already populated.
expectation: With PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH set and browsers present, launching a browser finds them.
reality: Playwright resolves the browser by revision, not by presence. A package version expecting revision N will not use the installed revision M, and the error it prints is a bordered box recommending `npx playwright install`. Following that advice is the failure mode recorded in cairn-0007 — so the error message steers you directly into the trap next door.
mechanism: Each playwright release pins an exact browser build. The preinstalled bundle satisfies whichever version the image was built against; an independently resolved npm install may not match it, and the remedy text is generic rather than aware of PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH.
workaround: Launch with an explicit executablePath pointing at the installed build (here `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome`) instead of downloading. List the browsers directory first to find the real revision. Do not follow the error's advice.

evidence.output:
║ Please run the following command to download new browsers: ║
║     npx playwright install                                 ║
evidence.note: Printed even though four browser bundles were already present at PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH.
Passing this path as executablePath launched successfully with no download.

check.confirmedIf: the launch fails recommending `npx playwright install` while browser bundles are already present at PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH
check.refutedIf: the launch succeeds using the preinstalled bundle, or the error acknowledges PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH and names the revision mismatch

observations.note: Hit while screenshotting this site. cairn-0007's workaround resolved it in one step — the first time a finding in this corpus saved time on unrelated work. Marked manual because the check requires installing a dependency this repo does not otherwise carry.
